title: Minnesota lawyer suspended over fake AI case citations

reading.body:
The headline indicates that a lawyer in Minnesota was suspended in connection with fake case citations attributed to AI use. This fits a recognized failure mode in legal practice: a generative AI system asserting fabricated case law as fact, and a lawyer submitting that output to a court without verifying the citations against actual legal databases or records.

The failure, if the headline accurately reflects events, would have occurred at the point of human review, meaning the output left the AI system and passed through the lawyer's hands before reaching a court without a check that would have caught the fabrications. That check, cross-referencing cited cases against official legal databases, is standard professional practice in legal work.

What is not established here is the full account of what happened, because the article body was not available for review. The suspension is noted in the headline, but the specific facts, the AI system involved, the exact citations at issue, and any formal findings by a disciplinary body, are not confirmed by the available material.
